```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
# Never download the full-text-search extension while building the vignette.
options(ausparl.auto_install_fts = FALSE, width = 90)
```

This vignette describes the database that ausparl queries: what it contains, how its tables fit
together, the identifiers that link them, and the conventions behind its columns. It is a
reference to keep open while you work; for a worked analysis see `vignette("ausparl")`.

Every example here runs on the small sample database bundled with the package (eight sitting
days), so the numbers are small. The full database has the same tables, views and columns.

```{r packages, message = FALSE}
library(ausparl)
library(dplyr)
db_connect(sample = TRUE)
```

## What is in the database

The database is one DuckDB file, `hansard.duckdb`, built from two sources:

- **Hansard**, the official record of debates in the House of Representatives and the Senate,
  from 1901. Each sitting day's transcript is parsed into its debates, subdebates and the
  individual contributions (*actions*) within them, and each speaker is matched to a member.
- **The Parliamentary Handbook** of the Commonwealth of Australia, which supplies the members
  and their service, parties, ministries and shadow ministries, committees, presiding officers,
  electorates, elections, parliaments and biographical detail.

`db_info()` reports which build you are connected to. Quote its `schema_version` and
`built_at` in your methods, so that others can reproduce your numbers.

```{r info}
db_info() |>
  select(schema_version, built_at, n_sittings, n_actions, n_members)
```

## How the tables fit together

The transcript tables nest, from the sitting day down to the single contribution:

```
sittings        one row per sitting day of one chamber
 └ debates      one row per debate within a sitting
    └ subdebates  one row per topic within a debate (subdebates can nest)
       └ actions  one row per contribution: a speech, question, answer,
                  interjection, quote or procedural note
```

The Handbook tables hang off two keys: `PHID`, which identifies a member, and the date. A turn
is linked to the member who made it through `actions.PHID`, and to what was true of that member
on the day (their party, role, electorate) through the sitting date.

```
members ── PHID ──┬── parl_service          seats held, with dates
                  ├── party_service         party memberships, with dates
                  ├── ministry_records      ministerial appointments
                  ├── shadow_ministry_records
                  ├── committee_members
                  ├── presiding_officers
                  └── occupations, qualifications, schools
```

## Identifiers

| Identifier | Identifies | Form | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sitting_id` | a sitting day of one chamber | `<chamber>_<date>` | `house_2002-10-15` |
| `debate_id` | a debate within a sitting | sitting id + `_D<n>` | `house_2002-10-15_D3` |
| `subdebate_id` | a subdebate within a debate | debate id + `_S<n>` | `house_2002-10-15_D3_S1` |
| `action_id` | one action (contribution) | sitting id + `_R<n>` | `house_2002-10-15_R12` |
| `PHID` | a member | Parliamentary Handbook id | `ZD4` (John Howard) |
| `parliament_id` | a parliament | its number | `40` (2002-2004) |
| `party_id` | a party | integer | see `get_parties()` |
| `electorate_id` | an electorate | integer | see `get_electorates()` |

Look a member's `PHID` up from their name with `find_member()`:

```{r find-member}
find_member("howard")
```

The sittings in the sample:

```{r sittings}
get_sittings()
```

A sitting's debates and subdebates:

```{r debates}
get_debates(sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15") |> head()
get_subdebates(debate_id = matches_pattern("house_2002-10-15_D%")) |> head()
```

## Actions and turns

`actions` is the core table: one row per contribution, with its text in `content`. Each action
has one `action_type`:

```{r action-types}
get_actions(columns = "action_type", collect = FALSE) |>
  count(action_type) |>
  collect()
```

- `speech`, `question` and `answer`: a member's own contribution.
- `quote`: a passage read into the record, such as a letter or petition: not the speaker's own
  words.
- `procedural`: a non-speech entry, such as "Mr Speaker took the chair".
- `unresolved_interjection`: an interjection whose speaker the source does not identify.

Logical flags refine the type. `is_speech`, `is_question` and `is_answer` mark a member's
substantive contributions, `is_interjection` marks interjections (including resolved ones,
which have `action_type = "speech"`), and `has_quote` marks actions that contain quoted
material. `get_speeches()` uses these flags: by default it returns speeches, questions and
answers, and leaves interjections out.

A speech interrupted by interjections, or continued across pages, is several actions. Actions
that belong to one uninterrupted contribution share a `turn_no`, and `get_speech_turns()`
merges them into a single row per turn:

```{r turns}
get_actions(
  sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15", is_non_speech = FALSE,
  columns = c("action_id", "turn_no", "PHID", "action_type", "is_interjection")
) |>
  arrange(turn_no) |>
  head(8)

get_speech_turns(sitting_id = "house_2002-10-15", include_text = FALSE) |>
  select(turn_no, n_actions, PHID, party_at_time, is_quote) |>
  head()
```

`get_sitting_timeline()` gives a sitting in document order, with the debate and subdebate
titles, and `get_interjections()` pairs each interjection with the turn it interrupted.

```{r timeline}
get_sitting_timeline(sitting_id = "senate_2019-11-26", include_text = FALSE) |>
  filter(action_type != "procedural") |>
  select(seq, debate_title, action_type, speaker_name) |>
  head(8)

get_interjections(chamber = "senate") |>
  select(date, interjector_name, target_name) |>
  head()
```

## Who spoke

Each action records the speaker as printed (`name_raw`, `party_raw`, `role_raw`,
`electorate_raw`) and, where they could be matched, the member's `PHID`. The `resolution`
column says how the speaker was matched:

| `resolution` | Meaning | `PHID` |
|---|---|---|
| `resolved` | matched to one member | set |
| `sentinel` | the presiding officer (Speaker, President or their deputy) in the chair | `NA` |
| `collective` | a group, such as "Honourable members" or "Opposition members" | `NA` |
| `unknown` | the source records the speaker as unknown | `NA` |
| `unmatched` | a named speaker who could not be matched to a member | `NA` |
| `ambiguous` | a name that fits more than one member | `NA` |
| `non_member` | someone who is not a member, such as the Governor-General | `NA` |
| `NA` | no speaker: procedural entries, and quotes that name no reader | `NA` |

```{r resolution}
get_actions(columns = "resolution", collect = FALSE) |>
  count(resolution) |>
  collect()
```

Presiding-officer turns are left out of `get_speeches()` unless `include_presiding = TRUE`, and
a `member` filter keeps only resolved turns.

## Context on the day

A member's party, role and electorate change over time, so the database holds them as dated
periods (`party_service`, `ministry_records`, `parl_service` and others). Views named
`v_<thing>_at_time` resolve them for each action on its sitting date, and the `add_*()`
functions join those views onto any result with an `action_id`:

| Function | Adds | From |
|---|---|---|
| `add_party()` | the speaker's party and its abbreviation | `v_party_at_time` |
| `add_role()` | minister, shadow minister or backbencher | `v_role_at_time` |
| `add_government_status()` | whether the speaker's party was in government | `v_government_status_at_time` |
| `add_electorate()` | the division or state the speaker represented | `v_electorate_at_time` |
| `add_age()` | age in years | `v_age_at_time` |
| `add_member()` | name, gender, state (not dated) | `members` |
| `add_debate()` | debate and subdebate titles | `debates`, `subdebates` |

```{r context}
get_speeches(from = "2002-10-15", to = "2002-10-15", chamber = "house",
             include_text = FALSE, limit = 5) |>
  add_party() |>
  add_government_status() |>
  select(action_id, PHID, party_abbrev_at_time, government_status_at_time)
```

Turns without a `PHID` get `NA` in every added column.

## Handbook tables and their conventions

The Handbook tables keep the Handbook's own column names (`DateStart`, `DisplayName`,
`MemberOrSenator`), so they read like the source. A few conventions apply across them:

- **`_raw` columns** keep a value as it was in the source, beside a cleaned version: for example
  `DateEnd_raw` beside `DateEnd`, or `name_raw` beside `PHID`. Use the cleaned column for
  analysis and the raw one to check it.
- **`handbook_flag`** marks rows where the Handbook itself looks wrong or inconsistent, such
  as overlapping terms. Flagged rows are kept, not corrected.
- **`*_status` and `date_uncertain`** describe how an end date was derived, or that a date is
  not known exactly.
- **An end date of `NA`** means the period is ongoing (or its end is not recorded).
- **Display views.** Several getters take `display = TRUE`, which reads a `v_<table>_display`
  view that adds readable columns, such as the member's `DisplayName` or the party colour.
- **`active_during`.** Getters for dated tables take `active_during`, which keeps the periods
  overlapping a year, a date or an `in_range()`.

```{r handbook}
get_party_service(PHID = "ZD4", display = TRUE)
get_ministry_records(PHID = "ZD4", active_during = 1996, display = TRUE) |>
  distinct(DisplayName, Role, Prep, Entity, RDateStart, RDateEnd)
```

Parties that merged, split or renamed are linked in `party_lineage`, and the spellings of party
names found in the transcripts are mapped to `party_id` in `party_alias`. Neither has a getter;
read them with `db_tbl()`:

```{r lineage}
db_tbl("party_lineage") |> collect()
```

## All tables and views

```{r catalog}
DBI::dbGetQuery(db_con(), "
  SELECT table_name AS name,
         CASE table_type WHEN 'VIEW' THEN 'view' ELSE 'table' END AS type
  FROM information_schema.tables
  WHERE table_schema = 'main'
  ORDER BY type, name
")
```

| Table | One row per | Getter |
|---|---|---|
| `sittings` | sitting day | `get_sittings()` |
| `debates` | debate | `get_debates()` |
| `subdebates` | subdebate | `get_subdebates()` |
| `actions` | action (contribution) | `get_actions()` |
| `provenance` | source file | `get_provenance()` |
| `members` | member | `get_members()` |
| `parliaments` | parliament | `get_parliaments()` |
| `parties` | party | `get_parties()` |
| `electorates` | electorate | `get_electorates()` |
| `elections` | election | `get_elections()` |
| `parl_service` | period of service in a seat | `get_parl_service()` |
| `party_service` | period of party membership | `get_party_service()` |
| `ministries` | ministry and governing party | `get_ministries()` |
| `ministry_records` | ministerial appointment | `get_ministry_records()` |
| `shadow_ministry_records` | shadow ministerial appointment | `get_shadow_ministry_records()` |
| `committee_members` | committee membership | `get_committee_members()` |
| `presiding_officers` | presiding office held | `get_presiding_officers()` |
| `occupations`, `qualifications`, `schools` | member and item | `get_occupations()`, `get_qualifications()`, `get_schools()` |
| `party_alias`, `party_lineage` | party name spelling; party relation | `db_tbl()` |
| `schema_version` | the build (one row) | `db_info()` |
| `parse_errors` | transcript that could not be parsed | `db_tbl()` |

The columns of any table or view are listed by `colnames(db_tbl("<name>"))`, and every getter's
help page lists its columns as filter arguments.

## Provenance

Every sitting can be traced to the transcript file it was parsed from, with the file's SHA-256
checksum and the parser generation that read it. `result_provenance()` does this for any
result:

```{r provenance}
get_speeches(from = "1902-10-10", to = "1902-10-10", include_text = FALSE, limit = 3) |>
  result_provenance()
```

```{r disconnect}
db_disconnect()
```
